newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil dismisses spillover to Asian forex woes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil dismisses spillover to Asian forex woes.

text.p: The Brazilian government does not fear any spillover from currency turmoil in Asia, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's spokesman said Monday.
Presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral told reporters the government did not fear a speculative attack on the real currency.

"There's nothing to cause concern in Brazil with regard to a speculative attack on the real," Amaral said at a regular briefing. "Attacks exist when the internal market reacts to a weakness in economic conditions, which is not the case in Brazil."

"It's important to realize that the fiscal situation and the trade balance are under control. The fiscal situation has improved since last year and there are indications of improvement in the trade balance."
Brazilian stocks slumped Monday, with traders attributing some of the sell-off to ripples from currency woes in Asia, where Thailand and the Philippines have been forced into de facto devaluations.
The currencies of Indonesia and Malaysia have also come under pressure.
Analysts say Brazil shares some of the aspects that have made those Asian countries vulnerable to speculation -- a widening current account gap and overvalued currency.
But Brazil also has $57 billion in reserves to ward off any speculative attack and its current account gap, at 4.2 percent of gross domestic product in the 12 months to June, is narrower.

Brazilian officials in fact are predicting that the troubles of their Asian competitors might even benefit Latin America's largest country, with jittery foreign invetsors seeking to park their funds elsewhere.
